meta.rule: Only entries with final_status APPROVED may be ingested; tier A1 and extractable text means ready. Tier A2 holds for a rights review. Image-only items wait for a human transcription and a second person's check. Nothing in candidates_pending_verification may be ingested: it is a to-do list for reviewers.
meta.ordering: contemporaneous before retrospective, then campaign-and-battle before campaign-only, then Union and Confederate alternating, then entry number

ready.citation: G. W. Beale, SHSP 11 (1883), p. N, via Internet Archive
ready.before_shipping: pass 1 named the Internet Archive item southernhistoricv11sout and pass 2 southernhistoric0011sout; the metadata API (this builder fetch, link-probe.json api.archive_org_metadata) shows both exist as separate scans of the Society Papers (596 and 594 images), which explains the two-leaf difference between the reviewers leaf-to-page maps. The preferred text is the original July 1883 issue scan; proof every passage against the page images because both OCR layers have errors

rights_basis.pass1: Text is a private letter of 1863 printed in SHSP vol. 11 whose own contents page reads 'January to December, 1883'; public domain by date. The IA metadata date field says 1876 (series start for every volume) and was not used. The linked gdg.org (Gettysburg Discussion Group) page is an unlicensed third-party transcription (last modified 2010) with a few textual differences, so the A1 tier applies to the SHSP text as read from the archive.org scan, not to the gdg copy.
rights_basis.pass2: Public domain by publication date, confirmed from the scans. The IA scan of vol. 11 has the title page 'JANUARY TO DECEMBER, 1883. RICHMOND, VA.: Rev. J. William Jones, D. D., Secretary Southern Historical Society'. A second scan, the original July issue, has the header 'Richmond, Va., July, 1883. No. 7.' Matter first published in 1883 is U.S. public domain. The IA vol. 11 item is a 1977 Kraus facsimile reprint (title page 'KRAUS REPRINT CO. Millwood, New York 1977'). A photographic reprint adds no new text rights, but the original-issue scan is the cleaner citation base. The gdg.org page carries no license or copyright notice: the host root, the /research/SHSP/ index and the page itself were checked, and the only 'permission' text is a photo credit on the home page. Its text is not a faithful copy of the print, so it should not be the quote source. The author's death date was not checked, so U.S. public-domain-by-date is the basis used and non-U.S. life-plus-years terms were not examined.

rights_basis.pass2: Unpublished 1863 manuscript by L. L. Polk (1837-1892 per UNC finding aid), so the author's life+70 term ended before 1963 and the letter is public domain in the US on the author-death basis, not an imprint-year basis. UNC finding aid for L.L. Polk Papers #3708 (fetched via the 301 chain to finding-aids.lib.unc.edu/catalog/03708): 'No usage restrictions', copyright 'retained by the authors ... or their descendants'. The blog page itself carries no license; it sends X-Robots-Tag: noarchive (an indexing hint, not a license). UNC owns the transcription/blog layer, so counsel should confirm before bulk reuse.

rights_basis.pass1: Underlying diary is an 1863 manuscript by an anonymous writer (unpublished diary; anonymous works are public domain 120 years after creation, so well past). The transcription was made by Frank Kline per the House Divided post (not stated in the PDF), and the diary is held by the Cumberland County Historical Society (CCHS) per the post and the file name; any copyright in the transcription is unstated. House Divided pages show '(c) Content 2007-2010 by Dickinson College' with no license for the PDF. Tier A2 pending review of the transcription terms.
rights_basis.pass2: Anonymous, unpublished 1863 diary; under 17 U.S.C. 302(c) a work made for no named author lasts 120 years from creation, which ended in 1983, so the diary is public domain. The PDF is a Word-made transcription by Frank Kline (per the House Divided post) of a manuscript held by the Cumberland County Historical Society (per the same post); neither the PDF nor the post gives a rights statement, and the Dickinson host asserts site copyright. Needs review of transcriber/CCHS terms.
